title: NEC Past Paper - Set 20 (2083 Asoj 17, 3rd shift)

questions.q: Plaster of Paris is obtained by calcining:
questions.s: Heating gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) to about 120-160 °C drives off three-quarters of its water and leaves the hemihydrate CaSO₄·½H₂O.
questions.trap: Limestone calcines to quicklime, which is lime and not plaster of Paris — the commonest substitution.
questions.trick: Plaster of Paris is a sulphate; limestone and dolomite are carbonates.

questions.q: The compound that gives cement its long-term (ultimate) strength is:
questions.s: Dicalcium silicate hydrates slowly and keeps contributing strength well past 28 days; C3S supplies the early strength.
questions.trap: C3S and C2S differ by one digit and by the whole of their timing.
questions.trick: The lower number hydrates later.

questions.q: The water absorption of a first-class brick should not exceed:
questions.s: A first-class brick absorbs no more than 15% of its dry weight after 24 hours of immersion; a second-class brick is allowed 20%.
questions.trap: 20% is the second-class limit and sits immediately beside it in the same table.
questions.trick: The better the class, the lower the absorption.

questions.q: In a cavity wall where both leaves are load-bearing, the effective thickness is taken as:
o: The greater of the stronger leaf alone or two-thirds of the sum of both
Half the sum of both leaves
questions.s: The cavity prevents the two leaves acting fully together, so only two-thirds of the combined thickness may be counted.
questions.trap: Adding both leaves assumes full composite action, which the cavity expressly prevents.
questions.trick: A cavity always costs you some of the combined thickness.
questions.mn: Two-thirds of the sum, or the stronger leaf.

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a triangular section about an axis through its centroid parallel to the base is:
questions.s: About the base it is bd³/12; shifting to the centroid at d/3 reduces it to bd³/36.
questions.trap: bd³/12 is correct for the triangle about its *base* and for the rectangle about its *centroid* — the same expression in two different roles.
questions.trick: Triangle: 12 about the base, 36 about the centroid.

questions.q: The error in levelling caused by the curvature of the earth is:
o: Positive, making observed staff readings too large
questions.s: The level line falls below the horizontal line of sight, so the staff reading is larger than the true difference; refraction partly offsets it.
questions.trap: Refraction acts in the opposite sense and is about one seventh as large, which makes the combined correction smaller but still positive.
questions.trick: Curvature reads high, refraction reads low, curvature wins.

questions.q: The volume of cement in a 50 kg bag is taken as:
questions.s: With a bulk density of about 1440 kg/m³, 50/1440 = 0.0347 m³, or roughly 35 litres.
questions.trap: The decimal place is the whole question — 0.0035 m³ is a tenth of the right value.
questions.trick: A bag is about 35 litres, roughly the volume of a bucket and a half.

questions.q: The arrangement provided to prevent moisture rising into a wall from the ground is a:
questions.s: A continuous impervious layer at plinth level blocks capillary rise from the foundation into the superstructure.
questions.trap: A plinth beam is at the same level and ties the structure together, but it does not stop moisture.
questions.trick: Same level, different purpose.

questions.q: The aggregate crushing value for a concrete wearing surface should not exceed:
questions.s: A wearing surface takes direct traffic, so the aggregate must be strong; 45% is permitted only for other concrete.
questions.trap: 45% is the general limit and is the number most often quoted.
questions.trick: Wearing surfaces always take the stricter limit.

questions.q: The principle of a plane table survey is that:
o: Plotting is done in the field at the same time as observation
Angles are measured and plotted later
questions.s: The table carries the drawing sheet, so rays are drawn as the detail is sighted and the plan grows on site.
questions.trap: A theodolite traverse also records directions, but the plotting happens afterwards in the office.
questions.trick: The whole advantage is that nothing is left to be plotted later.

questions.q: A soil with a liquid limit of 60 and a plastic limit of 25 has a plasticity index of:
questions.s: PI = LL − PL = 60 − 25 = 35, which places the soil in the high-plasticity clay range.
questions.trap: 85 is the sum rather than the difference and is the easiest slip to make under time pressure.
questions.trick: An index is always a difference between two limits.

questions.q: The relation between void ratio e and porosity n is:
questions.s: Void ratio refers voids to solids; porosity refers voids to the total volume, so the conversion divides by the solid fraction.
questions.trap: Inverting the expression gives n in terms of e, which is the companion formula n = e/(1 + e).
questions.trick: e can exceed 1; n never can — so the denominator must be (1 − n).

questions.q: The coefficient of permeability of a clean sand is of the order of:
questions.s: Sands run around 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁵ m/s; silts are near 10⁻⁷ and clays below 10⁻⁹.
questions.trap: 10⁻⁹ m/s is the clay value, and the exponents are easy to transpose.
questions.trick: Each step down in grain size drops the permeability by several orders of magnitude.

questions.q: The vane shear test is most suitable for:
questions.s: A four-bladed vane is pushed into soft clay and twisted; the torque at failure gives the undrained shear strength without sampling.
questions.trap: The direct shear box handles sand, and neither test works in gravel or rock.
questions.trick: A vane can only be pushed into something soft.

questions.q: The depth of the tension crack behind a retaining wall in cohesive soil is:
questions.s: Active pressure is negative over the top of the wall; setting it to zero gives the depth to which the soil cracks away.
questions.trap: 4c/γ is the *total* unsupported height, which is twice the crack depth for a vertical face in pure clay.
questions.trick: The crack is half the critical height.

questions.q: A raft foundation is preferred when the total footing area would exceed about:
o: 50% of the plan area of the building
questions.s: Beyond about half the plan area, individual footings nearly touch and a single raft is cheaper and performs better.
questions.trap: Waiting until 90% means building a raft in all but name, with the cost of formwork for separate footings.
questions.trick: When the footings nearly meet, join them.
questions.mn: Half the area, go to raft.

questions.q: The safe bearing capacity is obtained from the net ultimate bearing capacity by:
o: Dividing by the factor of safety and adding the overburden pressure
Multiplying by the factor of safety
questions.s: The net ultimate value is reduced by the factor of safety, then the overburden the soil already carried is added back to give a gross safe pressure.
questions.trap: Dividing alone gives the net *safe* capacity, which is one step short of the gross figure used in design.
questions.trick: Net safe plus overburden equals gross safe.
questions.mn: Divide, then add back the overburden.

questions.q: The standard Proctor test compacts soil in:
o: 3 layers with 25 blows of a 2.6 kg rammer
5 layers with 25 blows of a 4.9 kg rammer
questions.s: The modified test uses 5 layers and the heavier 4.9 kg rammer, which is why it gives a higher maximum dry density at a lower optimum moisture.
questions.trap: The modified Proctor figures are offered beside the standard ones and the two are routinely confused.
questions.trick: Standard 3 layers light rammer, modified 5 layers heavy rammer.

questions.q: In a flow net, the shape of each figure formed by flow lines and equipotential lines is approximately:
questions.s: Flow lines and equipotential lines intersect at right angles and are spaced so that each field is a curvilinear square, which is what makes Nf/Nd meaningful.
questions.trap: Any rectangle would satisfy the orthogonality condition, so only the square shape carries the discharge relation.
questions.trick: Equal drops of head across equal flow widths means a square.

questions.q: The angle of repose of a cohesionless soil is equal to its:
questions.s: A dry sand heap stands at the angle at which friction just balances gravity, which is the friction angle itself.
questions.trap: The failure plane is at 45° + φ/2, a different angle derived from the same φ.
questions.trick: A loose heap mobilises friction alone, so the slope angle is φ.

questions.q: The dynamic viscosity of water at 20 °C is approximately:
questions.s: About one centipoise. The *kinematic* viscosity at the same temperature is 1 × 10⁻⁶ m²/s.
questions.trap: 1 × 10⁻⁶ carries the right digits but belongs to kinematic viscosity, and the units give it away.
questions.trick: Dynamic is in Pa·s; kinematic is in m²/s.

questions.q: The centre of pressure on a vertical plane surface always lies:
o: Below the centroid of the surface
questions.s: Pressure increases with depth, so the resultant acts lower than the geometric centre; the offset is I/(A·h̄).
questions.trap: For a horizontal surface the two coincide, because the pressure is uniform — but the question specifies vertical.
questions.trick: More pressure lower down pulls the resultant down.
questions.mn: Centre of pressure is always deeper.

questions.q: A venturimeter measures discharge by:
o: Creating a pressure difference at a contraction
Timing the fill of a tank
questions.s: The throat accelerates the flow and lowers the pressure; the difference between inlet and throat gives the discharge through Bernoulli and continuity.
questions.trap: An orifice meter works on the same principle but with a sharp plate and a much larger head loss.
questions.trick: No moving parts, just a measured pressure drop.

questions.q: The friction factor for laminar flow in a circular pipe is:
questions.s: In the laminar range the Darcy friction factor depends only on the Reynolds number, as f = 64/Re.
questions.trap: 16/Re is the *Fanning* friction factor, which is one quarter of the Darcy value — the commonest confusion in pipe flow.
questions.trick: Darcy 64, Fanning 16; the ratio is four.

questions.q: The critical depth in a rectangular channel carrying a discharge per unit width q is:
questions.s: Setting the Froude number to one and solving gives yc as the cube root of q squared over g.
questions.trap: The square root appears in so many hydraulic formulas that the cube root is easily replaced by it.
questions.trick: Critical depth is a cube root, every time.

questions.q: The runoff coefficient C in the rational formula for a paved urban area is about:
questions.s: Paved surfaces absorb almost nothing, so most of the rain runs off; cultivated land is nearer 0.3 and forest lower still.
questions.trap: A value above 1 is impossible, since runoff cannot exceed rainfall.
questions.trick: The more impervious the surface, the nearer C is to one.

questions.q: Surface tension of a liquid has the units:
questions.s: It is a force acting along a line of contact, so it is measured as force per unit length — equivalently energy per unit area.
questions.trap: N/m² is pressure, and the two are routinely interchanged because both involve force and area.
questions.trick: Tension acts along a line, not over an area.

questions.q: The momentum correction factor β for laminar flow in a pipe is:
questions.s: For a parabolic laminar profile β = 4/3 and the energy correction factor α = 2; in turbulent flow both approach unity.
questions.trap: 2.0 is the *energy* correction factor for the same profile, and the two are offered together.
questions.trick: α is always larger than β for the same profile.

questions.q: Water hammer pressure rise is reduced by:
questions.s: If closure takes longer than 2L/C the reflected wave returns before the valve is shut and relieves part of the rise.
questions.trap: Rapid closure feels safer because it stops the flow sooner; it produces the maximum possible surge.
questions.trick: Compare the closure time with the wave travel time 2L/C.
questions.mn: Slow the valve, save the pipe.

questions.q: The specific energy in an open channel is a minimum at:
questions.s: The specific energy curve has a single minimum, and the depth at which it occurs is the critical depth.
questions.trap: Normal depth is where the flow is uniform for a given slope and has nothing to do with the minimum.
questions.trick: Minimum specific energy and Fr = 1 are the same condition.

questions.q: For a cantilever carrying a uniformly distributed load w over its length L, the maximum bending moment is:
questions.s: It occurs at the fixed end, where the whole load wL acts at its centroid L/2 from the support.
questions.trap: wL²/8 is the simply supported case, and it is the most-quoted bending moment in the subject.
questions.trick: A cantilever carries four times the moment of a simple beam of the same span and load.

questions.q: The relation between the three elastic constants is:
questions.s: For an isotropic material the shear modulus, Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio are tied by E = 2G(1 + μ).
questions.trap: E = 3K(1 − 2μ) is the companion relation involving bulk modulus, and the signs differ between the two.
questions.trick: The shear relation has a plus sign; the bulk relation has a minus.

questions.q: The radius of gyration of a section is:
questions.s: It is the distance at which the whole area could be concentrated without changing the moment of inertia, and it has the dimension of length.
questions.trap: I/A has the dimension of length squared, so it cannot be a radius.
questions.trick: Check the dimensions: a radius must come out in metres.
questions.mn: Radius of gyration k = √(I/A), and it is a length.

questions.q: A plane truss with m members, r reactions and j joints is determinate when:
questions.s: Each joint provides two equations of equilibrium in a plane, so the unknowns (members plus reactions) must equal 2j.
questions.trap: 3j is the equivalent count for a rigid *frame*, where each joint also resists moment.
questions.trick: Pin joints give two equations each; rigid joints give three.

questions.q: The influence line for the bending moment at a section of a simply supported beam is:
o: A triangle with its peak under that section
A trapezium with its peak at mid-span
questions.s: The ordinate is ab/L, zero at both supports and greatest when the unit load stands directly over the section.
questions.trap: A parabola is the *bending moment diagram* for a UDL, which is a different diagram answering a different question.
questions.trick: Influence line for moment: always triangular on a simple span.

questions.q: The degree of static indeterminacy of a fixed beam is:
questions.s: Each fixed end gives three reaction components, making six in all, against three equations of equilibrium.
questions.trap: A propped cantilever is indeterminate to degree 1 and a continuous two-span beam to degree 1 as well.
questions.trick: Count the reactions and subtract three.

questions.q: Poisson's ratio for most metals lies between:
questions.s: Steel is about 0.3 and concrete about 0.15; the theoretical maximum for an isotropic material is 0.5, reached by rubber.
questions.trap: 0.5 is the limiting value for an incompressible material and is easily taken as typical.
questions.trick: A value of 0.5 would mean no volume change at all.

questions.q: The shear force diagram for a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load is:
o: A straight line sloping from +wL/2 to −wL/2
A triangle with its peak at mid-span
questions.s: Integrating a constant load gives a linear shear force, which crosses zero at mid-span where the moment is greatest.
questions.trap: The *bending moment* diagram for the same loading is the parabola, and the two diagrams are easily swapped.
questions.trick: Each integration raises the order by one: load constant, shear linear, moment parabolic.

questions.q: In a beam of rectangular section, the maximum shear stress is:
questions.s: The parabolic shear stress distribution peaks at the neutral axis at 1.5 times the mean value V/A.
questions.trap: 4/3 is the corresponding factor for a *circular* section, and the two are the standard pair.
questions.trick: Rectangle 1.5, circle 1.33.

questions.q: Castigliano's first theorem gives the deflection as:
o: The partial derivative of strain energy with respect to the load
The integral of the bending moment
The second moment of the M/EI diagram
The product of load and length
questions.s: ∂U/∂P gives the deflection in the direction of P, which is the quickest route for a single applied load.
questions.trap: The moment-area theorems use the M/EI diagram and are the alternative approach to the same problem.
questions.trick: Differentiate the energy with respect to the force you want the deflection under.

questions.q: The partial safety factor for concrete in the limit state of collapse is:
questions.s: Concrete takes 1.5 and steel 1.15, because concrete strength is more variable and its failure less ductile.
questions.trap: 1.15 is the steel factor, and the two sit side by side in the same clause.
questions.trick: The more variable material gets the larger factor.

questions.q: The slump test measures:
questions.s: The cone is filled, lifted and the subsidence measured; a larger slump means a more workable (wetter) mix.
questions.trap: Workability correlates loosely with water content and hence inversely with strength, which invites the wrong inference.
questions.trick: The test is on fresh concrete, so it cannot measure any hardened property.

questions.q: The limiting depth of the neutral axis for Fe415 steel as a fraction of the effective depth is:
questions.s: xu,max/d is 0.53 for Fe250, 0.48 for Fe415 and 0.46 for Fe500 — the limit falls as the steel gets stronger.
questions.trap: All three values appear in the same table, and the grade must be matched to the right one.
questions.trick: Stronger steel yields at a higher strain, so the neutral axis limit drops.

questions.q: The maximum spacing of main reinforcement in a slab is the lesser of:
o: 3 times the effective depth or 300 mm
2 times the effective depth or 450 mm
5 times the effective depth or 300 mm
questions.s: IS 456 limits main steel spacing to 3d or 300 mm; distribution steel may go to 5d or 450 mm.
questions.trap: 5d or 450 mm is the limit for the *distribution* bars, and the two rules sit in the same clause.
questions.trick: Main steel is held tighter than distribution steel.

questions.q: The minimum pitch of rivets or bolts in a steel connection is:
questions.s: Closer spacing would make the holes interfere and leave too little metal between them to carry the bearing stress.
questions.trap: 16t and 12t are *maximum* pitch rules for the same connection, expressed in plate thickness instead.
questions.trick: The minimum is in bolt diameters; the maximum is in plate thicknesses.

questions.q: The permissible compressive stress in timber depends chiefly on:
o: The direction of the grain relative to the load
The length of the member only
questions.s: Timber is far stronger along the grain than across it, so the stress permitted parallel to the grain is several times the perpendicular value.
questions.trap: Slenderness also reduces the permissible stress, but the governing property of the material is its anisotropy.
questions.trick: Timber is a bundle of fibres; pushing along them is quite different from pushing across them.

questions.q: Curing of concrete should normally continue for at least:
questions.s: Seven days of moist curing for OPC and ten to fourteen for blended cements; the strength at 28 days is the design figure, not the curing period.
questions.trap: 28 days is when the characteristic strength is measured, which makes it the obvious but wrong answer for curing.
questions.trick: Curing period and testing age are different things.

questions.q: In a one-way slab, the main reinforcement runs:
questions.s: The load spans the shorter way, so the main steel is placed in that direction and distribution steel runs the long way.
questions.trap: A slab is "one-way" when the long side is more than twice the short side, which invites the idea that it spans the long way.
questions.trick: A plate always spans the shortest distance to its supports.
questions.mn: Main steel on the short span.

questions.q: The effective length of a steel column fixed at both ends is:
questions.s: IS 800 gives 0.65L for both ends fixed in practice, against the theoretical 0.5L, recognising that real fixity is never complete.
questions.trap: 0.5L is the theoretical value and appears in every mechanics textbook, which makes it the natural answer.
questions.trick: Codes use conservative effective lengths above the theoretical ones.

questions.q: Development length of a reinforcing bar is required to:
o: Transfer the bar force to the surrounding concrete by bond
questions.s: Ld = φσs/(4τbd) — the length over which bond stress can develop the full design stress in the bar.
questions.trap: Anchorage at a support is a particular application of development length, not a different requirement.
questions.trick: A bar can only carry what the surrounding concrete can grip.

questions.q: The permissible limit of fluoride in drinking water in Nepal is:
questions.s: Below about 0.5 mg/l causes dental caries and above 1.5 mg/l causes fluorosis, so there is both a lower and an upper bound.
questions.trap: Fluoride is the rare parameter with a desirable *minimum*, which makes a single small number look wrong.
questions.trick: Too little and too much are both harmful.

questions.q: The service reservoir in a water supply system is sized to store about:
o: One-third of the maximum daily demand
questions.s: Roughly a third of the day's supply balances the difference between steady pumping and fluctuating consumption, with an allowance for fire and breakdown.
questions.trap: A larger store sounds safer but costs more and lets the water age, which risks the chlorine residual.
questions.trick: The reservoir balances hours of variation, not weeks.
questions.mn: About a third of a day.

questions.q: The optimum pH for coagulation with alum is about:
questions.s: Aluminium hydroxide is least soluble in that range, so the floc forms readily; outside it the alum stays dissolved.
questions.trap: Lime softening works at a much higher pH, around 9-11, which is a different process in the same works.
questions.trick: Coagulation happens near neutral pH.

questions.q: The minimum diameter of a public sewer is normally:
questions.s: Anything smaller blocks too easily and cannot be cleaned by rodding; house connections may be 100 mm.
questions.trap: 100 mm is the house drain size and is the figure carried across from plumbing practice.
questions.trick: A public sewer must admit a cleaning rod and tolerate rubbish.

questions.q: The sludge volume index (SVI) of a well-settling activated sludge is about:
questions.s: An SVI in that range settles and compacts well; above about 150 the sludge bulks and carries over the final weir.
questions.trap: A larger number sounds like a larger, healthier floc; it actually means a bulking, poorly settling sludge.
questions.trick: A low SVI means the sludge occupies little volume, which is what is wanted.

questions.q: An initial environmental examination in Nepal is required for a project that is:
o: Smaller in scale than one requiring a full EIA
Larger than one requiring an EIA
questions.s: The Environment Protection Rules set thresholds: projects below them need an IEE, those above need an EIA.
questions.trap: Projects in protected areas may need an EIA regardless of size, which is an exception rather than the rule.
questions.trick: IEE is the lighter study for the smaller project.

questions.q: The most reliable indicator organism for faecal contamination of water is:
questions.s: E. coli lives only in the intestine of warm-blooded animals, so its presence points specifically to faecal pollution.
questions.trap: Total coliforms include soil and plant organisms, so their presence is suggestive rather than conclusive.
questions.trick: The more specific the organism, the better the indicator.

questions.q: Breakpoint chlorination is the dose at which:
o: All ammonia has been oxidised and free residual chlorine begins to appear
Taste and odour are at a maximum
questions.s: Chlorine first forms chloramines, which are then destroyed; past the breakpoint the residual is free chlorine and disinfection is reliable.
questions.trap: Taste and odour actually peak just *before* the breakpoint, which makes under-dosing worse than not dosing at all.
questions.trick: Dose past the breakpoint or not at all.

questions.q: The main purpose of a septic tank is:
o: Sedimentation and anaerobic digestion of settled solids
questions.s: It settles the solids and digests them anaerobically; the liquid effluent still needs a soak pit or a drain field.
questions.trap: A septic tank is often treated as complete treatment, which is why so many discharge polluted effluent.
questions.trick: A septic tank is a first stage, not a treatment works.
questions.mn: Settle and digest, then soak away.

questions.q: The duty of water is expressed in:
questions.s: Duty is the area a unit discharge can irrigate through the base period; delta is the equivalent depth in metres.
questions.trap: Delta is measured in metres and base period in days, so each of the other options belongs to a related quantity.
questions.trick: Duty is an area per discharge; delta is a depth.

questions.q: Lacey's regime perimeter for a discharge Q is given by:
questions.s: The regime wetted perimeter is 4.75 times the square root of the discharge in cumecs.
questions.trap: 0.47 belongs to the scour depth formula and 1.76 to the silt factor — three constants from the same theory.
questions.trick: Perimeter 4.75, scour 0.47, silt factor 1.76.

questions.q: Bligh's creep theory assumes that the loss of head along the seepage path is:
o: Uniform per unit length of creep
Proportional to the square of the length
questions.s: Bligh made no distinction between vertical and horizontal creep; Lane later weighted horizontal lengths at one third.
questions.trap: Lane's weighted creep theory is the refinement, and its weighting is exactly what Bligh lacked.
questions.trick: Bligh is the simple uniform theory; Lane adds the weighting.

questions.q: A launching apron is provided to:
o: Fall into a scour hole and protect the foundation
Carry the canal over a drain
questions.s: Loose stone laid beyond the structure slides down as the bed scours, forming a protective slope over the exposed face.
questions.trap: A rigid apron would be undermined by the same scour the launching apron is designed to follow.
questions.trick: The apron is meant to move; that is the point of it.

questions.q: A super-passage is a cross-drainage work in which:
o: The drain is carried over the canal
The canal is carried over the drain
The two are allowed to mix
The canal passes through a siphon
questions.s: Drain over canal is a super-passage; canal over drain is an aqueduct. The names give no clue, so they must be learnt.
questions.trap: The aqueduct is the mirror image and is the better-known of the two.
questions.trick: "Super" refers to the drain passing above.

questions.q: The depth of a tile drain below the ground surface is governed by:
o: The depth of the root zone to be kept free of water
questions.s: The drain must hold the water table below the root zone, so its depth follows the crop's rooting depth and the required freeboard.
questions.trap: Rainfall intensity governs the *spacing* and capacity of the drains rather than their depth.
questions.trick: Depth protects the roots; spacing handles the volume.

questions.q: The base period of a crop is:
o: The total period from first watering to last watering
The period of maximum growth only
The time between two consecutive waterings
questions.s: It runs from the first watering before sowing to the last before harvest, and it appears in the duty-delta relation.
questions.trap: The crop period is slightly longer, running from sowing to harvest, and the two are often used interchangeably.
questions.trick: Base period is measured by waterings, crop period by the plant.

questions.q: Kennedy's critical velocity is the velocity that:
o: Keeps the channel free from both silting and scouring
questions.s: Kennedy derived it from non-silting, non-scouring channels on the Upper Bari Doab, as V₀ = 0.55 m y^0.64.
questions.trap: "Critical velocity" in open channel hydraulics means the velocity at Fr = 1, which is an entirely different idea.
questions.trick: Kennedy's critical velocity is a regime condition, not a Froude condition.

questions.q: A fish ladder is provided at a diversion headworks to:
o: Allow fish to migrate past the barrier
questions.s: A series of stepped pools with a controlled velocity lets fish ascend past the weir to their spawning grounds.
questions.trap: It looks like an energy dissipating structure because of the stepped pools, which is a by-product rather than the purpose.
questions.trick: The ladder exists for the fish, not for the water.

questions.q: A run-of-river hydropower plant:
o: Has little or no storage and depends on the river flow
questions.s: Generation follows the hydrograph, so output falls in the dry season; pondage may give a few hours of daily regulation.
questions.trap: A peaking run-of-river plant with pondage does follow the daily peak, which blurs the distinction with a storage plant.
questions.trick: No reservoir means no control over the season.
questions.mn: Run of river, run of the flow.

questions.q: The load factor of a power plant is the ratio of:
questions.s: A high load factor means a steady demand, which lets the same plant serve more units and lowers the cost per unit.
questions.trap: Average load to installed capacity is the *capacity* factor, the neighbouring ratio.
questions.trick: Load factor compares two demands; capacity factor compares demand with plant.

questions.q: The free board of an earthen dam is measured from:
o: The maximum reservoir level to the top of the dam
The river bed to the crest
The minimum pool level to the crest
The spillway crest to the river bed
questions.s: Free board is the margin above the highest water level that keeps waves and settlement from overtopping the embankment.
questions.trap: Measuring from the normal reservoir level overstates the margin and ignores the flood rise.
questions.trick: Free board protects against the worst case, so it starts at the highest level.
questions.mn: From the maximum water level up.

questions.q: A side intake on a river is normally located:
o: On the outer bank of a bend, where the flow is deep and sediment-free
On the inner bank of a bend
At the centre of a straight reach bed
At the confluence of two rivers
questions.s: Secondary currents at a bend sweep the bed load towards the inner bank and leave the outer bank deep and relatively clean.
questions.trap: The inner bank looks safer because the current is gentler there, which is exactly why it silts up.
questions.trick: Sediment goes to the inside of the bend; the intake goes to the outside.

questions.q: A surge tank is NOT required when:
o: The headrace is a short open channel or the penstock is very short
The plant operates at base load
questions.s: Surge protection is needed when a long pressurised conduit must decelerate; a short penstock or a free-surface channel has nowhere to build a surge.
questions.trap: High head and large discharge both increase the surge, so they are reasons *for* a surge tank, not against it.
questions.trick: Surge needs a long column of water under pressure.

questions.q: A Francis turbine is classified as:
questions.s: Water enters radially and leaves axially, and the pressure falls through the runner, which makes it a mixed-flow reaction machine.
questions.trap: Pelton is the tangential impulse turbine and Kaplan the axial reaction one — the three are always offered together.
questions.trick: Francis changes direction inside the runner, hence mixed flow.

questions.q: Secondary power in a hydropower scheme is the power:
o: Available only during the high-flow season
questions.s: It is the surplus above firm power, available when the river is in flood, and it is sold at a lower rate because it cannot be relied upon.
questions.trap: "Secondary" sounds like a smaller unit of plant rather than a seasonal surplus.
questions.trick: Firm is what you can promise; secondary is what you happen to have.

questions.q: The purpose of a cut-off trench under an earthen dam is to:
o: Intercept seepage through the pervious foundation
Increase the weight of the dam
questions.s: The trench is excavated to an impervious stratum and backfilled with compacted clay, lengthening the seepage path and reducing the gradient.
questions.trap: A toe drain controls seepage too, but it collects water that has already passed rather than preventing it.
questions.trick: The cut-off stops seepage; the drain handles what gets through.
questions.mn: Cut it off at the foundation.

questions.q: The width of the right of way for a national highway in plain terrain in Nepal is about:
questions.s: The Nepal Road Standard reserves 50 m for a national highway in plain terrain, narrower in hills where land is costly to acquire.
questions.trap: The carriageway itself is only about 7 m, and that figure is the one visualised on site.
questions.trick: Right of way is the land reserved, not the road built.

questions.q: Superelevation on a horizontal curve is provided to:
o: Counteract the centrifugal force on a vehicle
questions.s: Raising the outer edge lets a component of the vehicle's weight act towards the centre of the curve and relieves the side friction.
questions.trap: Camber drains the carriageway on a straight, and superelevation looks like a steeper camber.
questions.trick: Camber drains, superelevation steers.

questions.q: The ductility of bitumen is measured as:
o: The distance in cm a briquette stretches before breaking
The temperature at which it flows
questions.s: A standard briquette is pulled at 50 mm/min at 27 °C and the elongation at break is the ductility, usually at least 50 cm.
questions.trap: Needle penetration is the neighbouring test on the same material and measures hardness instead.
questions.trick: Ductility is about stretching; penetration is about pushing in.

questions.q: The design hourly volume for a highway is usually taken as the:
o: 30th highest hourly volume of the year
Highest hourly volume of the year
questions.s: Designing for the absolute peak would be uneconomical for a few hours a year; the 30th highest hour is the accepted compromise.
questions.trap: The highest hourly volume is the natural reading of "design for the peak" and is deliberately not used.
questions.trick: The curve of hourly volumes flattens sharply after about the 30th hour.

questions.q: The modulus of subgrade reaction k is determined by the:
questions.s: A 750 mm plate is loaded and the pressure divided by the 1.25 mm settlement gives k, which is used in rigid pavement design.
questions.trap: CBR is the subgrade test for *flexible* pavements, and the two are the standard pairing.
questions.trick: Rigid pavement needs k; flexible needs CBR.

questions.q: A seal coat is applied to a bituminous surface to:
o: Waterproof the surface and improve skid resistance
Act as a bond between layers
questions.s: It is a thin final application that closes the surface voids; it adds no structural strength.
questions.trap: A tack coat bonds layers and a prime coat treats the base — three thin bituminous applications with three different jobs.
questions.trick: The seal coat is always the last one applied.
questions.mn: Prime below, tack between, seal on top.

questions.q: Extra widening on a horizontal curve is provided because:
o: The rear wheels track inside the front wheels and drivers need more room
The superelevation reduces the usable width
The pavement is weaker on a curve
questions.s: It has a mechanical part, from off-tracking of the rear axle, and a psychological part, because drivers steer less precisely on a curve.
questions.trap: Superelevation is provided on the same curve, which makes it look like the cause of the widening.
questions.trick: A long vehicle sweeps a wider path through a bend than its own width.

questions.q: A rotary intersection is most suitable when:
o: Traffic volumes are moderate and approaches are roughly equal
One approach carries far more traffic than the others
Volumes are very high on all approaches
questions.s: Weaving needs gaps in the circulating flow; one dominant approach or very high total volume destroys those gaps and the rotary locks up.
questions.trap: A rotary looks like the answer to a busy junction, when heavy traffic is exactly what it cannot handle.
questions.trick: Rotaries work on give-way, which needs gaps.
questions.mn: Moderate and balanced, or not at all.

questions.q: A contraction joint in a rigid pavement is provided to:
o: Control cracking caused by shrinkage and temperature fall
questions.s: A groove about a quarter of the slab depth creates a plane of weakness so the inevitable crack forms where it can be sealed.
questions.trap: Expansion joints allow growth in hot weather and are the opposite member of the same family.
questions.trick: Concrete shrinks far more than it expands, so contraction joints are the commoner ones.
questions.mn: Contract to crack where you choose.

questions.q: The recommended thickness ratio of a dimension line to an outline in engineering drawing is:
o: Dimension lines are thinner than outlines
questions.s: Outlines are drawn thick so the object reads clearly; dimension, extension and centre lines are thin so they do not compete with it.
questions.trap: Both at the same weight makes the drawing flat and much harder to read at a glance.
questions.trick: The object should dominate the sheet.
questions.mn: Thick for the object, thin for the notes.

questions.q: The present worth of a uniform annual amount A over n years at interest i is found using the:
questions.s: It converts a series of equal payments into one equivalent sum today; the capital recovery factor is its reciprocal.
questions.trap: The capital recovery factor goes the other way, converting a present sum into an annual payment.
questions.trick: Ask which direction the conversion runs: series to present, or present to series.
questions.mn: Series to present, that is P/A.

questions.q: In PERT, the expected time of an activity is:
questions.s: The beta distribution weights the most likely time four times as heavily as the optimistic and pessimistic estimates.
questions.trap: A simple average of the three ignores that the most likely time is far better information than the extremes.
questions.trick: Six in the denominator: 1 + 4 + 1.
questions.mn: o plus four m plus p, over six.

questions.q: The purpose of a bar bending schedule is to:
o: List the shape, size, length and number of every reinforcing bar
questions.s: It lets the steel be cut and bent off site, gives an accurate quantity for ordering and payment, and prevents waste.
questions.trap: A reinforcement drawing shows where the bars go; the schedule tabulates what they are.
questions.trick: The drawing is the picture; the schedule is the list.

questions.q: An engineer who signs drawings prepared by someone else without checking them:
o: Breaches professional ethics by certifying work not verified
Acts properly if the other person is qualified
Is exempt if a fee is not charged
Has no responsibility for the content
questions.s: A signature is a certification that the work has been done or checked by the signer, and the responsibility that follows cannot be delegated.
questions.trap: Relying on a qualified colleague sounds reasonable until something fails, when the signature is what is examined.
questions.trick: A signature transfers responsibility to the signer.
questions.mn: Sign only what you have checked.

questions.q: An engineer whose registration has been cancelled by the NEC may:
o: Practise only in the private sector
questions.s: Registration is the license to practise, so cancelling it removes the entitlement entirely.
questions.trap: Supervision mitigates inexperience, not the absence of a license.
questions.trick: No registration, no practice — there is no partial state.

questions.q: Crashing a project means:
o: Shortening the duration by adding resources at extra cost
Extending the duration to save cost
questions.s: Activities on the critical path are accelerated until the saving in indirect cost no longer covers the extra direct cost.
questions.trap: The word suggests failure rather than deliberate acceleration.
questions.trick: Crashing always costs money and always targets the critical path.

questions.q: The salvage value of an asset is:
o: Its expected value at the end of its useful life
Its value halfway through its life
questions.s: It is subtracted from the first cost to give the depreciable amount in every depreciation method.
questions.trap: Scrap value assumes the asset is broken up for materials, which is the lower of the two figures.
questions.trick: Salvage assumes it can still be sold; scrap assumes it cannot.
questions.mn: What it is worth when you are done with it.

questions.q: The defect liability period in a construction contract is the period during which:
o: The contractor must make good defects at their own cost
The contractor may not start work
The design may be changed freely
questions.s: It runs from completion, usually for twelve months, and the retention money is released only at the end of it.
questions.trap: It is sometimes taken as a warranty against all failure; it covers defects in the contractor's own work, not the designer's.
questions.trick: The period protects the employer against bad workmanship after handover.
questions.mn: Defects fixed free, for a year.

questions.q: In orthographic projection, the minimum number of views normally required to describe a simple object is:
questions.s: Two views fix all three dimensions for most simple shapes; a third is added when a feature is otherwise ambiguous.
questions.trap: Six views are possible and are shown in the textbook diagram, which makes six look like the standard.
questions.trick: Each view gives two of the three dimensions, so two views cover all three.
questions.mn: Two usually, three when in doubt.

questions.q: Conflict of interest arises when an engineer:
o: Has a personal interest that could influence professional judgement
Works on two projects at once
questions.s: The duty is to disclose the interest and withdraw from the decision; the conflict exists whether or not the judgement is actually affected.
questions.trap: Disagreement and multiple projects are ordinary professional life and raise no ethical issue by themselves.
questions.trick: Ask whether a reasonable observer would doubt the engineer's impartiality.

questions.q: Cavitation in a reaction turbine is avoided by limiting the:
o: Setting height of the runner above the tailrace
questions.s: If the runner is set too high the pressure at its exit falls to the vapour pressure and bubbles form; Thoma’s cavitation factor fixes the permissible height.
questions.trap: A longer draft tube recovers more head, which makes the draft tube sound like the controlling element rather than the setting.
questions.trick: Cavitation is a pressure problem, and pressure at the runner depends on how high it sits.

questions.q: A sluice valve in a water main is used to:
o: Isolate a section of the main for repair
questions.s: Sluice (gate) valves are placed at intervals and at branches so a length of main can be shut off without emptying the whole system.
questions.trap: A reflux valve prevents reverse flow and an air valve releases air — three valves on the same main with three duties.
questions.trick: A gate valve is either open or shut; it is for isolation, not regulation.

questions.q: The main consequence of a rising water table in an irrigated area is:
o: Reduced aeration of the root zone and falling crop yield
questions.s: Roots need air as well as water; once the water table reaches the root zone the soil is saturated and the crop suffers.
questions.trap: More water sounds beneficial for a crop, which is exactly why waterlogging is under-recognised by farmers.
questions.trick: Saturated soil has no air left in its voids.
questions.mn: Saturated soil has no air, so the roots drown.

questions.q: In the third twenty-year road development plan, roads are classified by:
o: Function and the administrative authority responsible
questions.s: Nepal classifies its roads as national highways, feeder roads, district roads and urban roads, each with its own responsible authority and standard.
questions.trap: Pavement type and width follow from the classification rather than defining it.
questions.trick: The class decides who builds and maintains the road.
